summary: Pulse of Earth is an interactive experience that turns Earth images into sound. Explore the included NASA nighttime-light visualizations, choose a musical style, and hear image brightness translated into notes. A spinning globe leads to five short challenges: find bright signals, compare tones, collect glowing targets, and answer questions about the images. An original guide character introduces the experience, while English and Arabic interface options and accessibility controls make it easier to explore. The project brings together music, maps, and playful learning to spark curiosity about our planet. Nighttime-light maps are the NASA images embedded in this version; other listed topics use labeled illustrative placeholders.
details:
Pulse of Earth: Transforming Environmental Data into Interactive Sound and Touch

Project Overview

The idea behind Pulse of Earth started with a simple question: how can we make complex environmental data feel real and accessible to everyone?

Instead of presenting satellite readings, temperature shifts, and natural phenomena as raw numbers or abstract charts, this project turns environmental metrics into an interactive sensory experience through sound, touch, and visuals. When a user selects a location or metric, the platform translates those numbers into musical tones—incorporating elements like traditional Middle Eastern scales (such as Rast, Bayati, and Nahawand)—alongside visual elements and subtle haptic feedback. By giving data a voice, we transform dry information into something you can listen to and feel.

Target Audience & Accessibility for the Visually Impaired

While the platform is open to students, researchers, and anyone interested in the environment, it was built with a clear focus on accessibility for visually impaired users and people with determination:

  • Sound and Touch as Primary Interfaces: Since visually impaired individuals rely heavily on auditory and tactile cues, translating climate data into musical variations and device vibrations (haptic feedback) lets users "hear" temperature trends and "feel" environmental shifts without needing to view complex graphs.
  • Inclusive Interface Design: The platform integrates screen-reader compatibility, voice control, and clean navigation so that exploring scientific data is straightforward and independent for every user.

Key Benefits & Expected Impact

  • Simplifying Complex Science: It turns heavy scientific datasets into clear, engaging auditory patterns.
  • Equal Access to Science: It opens up environmental research and space data to people who are blind or visually impaired, proving that learning tools can be truly inclusive.
  • Raising Environmental Awareness: Connecting data to sound creates an intuitive, memorable experience that helps people connect with what is happening to our planet.

Tools, Languages, & Technologies

  • Web & Programming: HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript for structural layout, styling, and real-time interaction handling.
  • Graphics & Audio Engines: HTML5 Canvas for rendering visual elements and the Web Audio API for real-time sound generation and frequency mapping.
  • Design & Usability: Clean layout tools focused on high-contrast visuals, clean typography, and UI standards tailored for assistive technologies.
  • Hardware Support: Built to run on standard computers, tablets, and smartphones, leveraging built-in vibration motors for haptic responses on mobile devices.

Creative Highlights

  • Data Sonification: Using authentic musical structures to represent scientific shifts gives the project a distinct artistic identity.
  • Multi-Sensory Engagement: Combining visual representation, real-time sound, and physical vibration ensures users experience the data through more than just text on a screen.
  • Focus on Universal Design: Inclusive features were integrated right from the start rather than added as an afterthought.

Practical Considerations During Development

  • Performance & Speed: Optimizing code so audio rendering and visual transitions remain fast and smooth across different devices.
  • Data Accuracy: Ensuring that pitch shifts and auditory cues directly correspond to actual environmental metrics so the experience remains educational and reliable.
  • User Comfort: Balancing sound levels, tones, and visual contrast to create a smooth, engaging experience without causing fatigue.
